routes.label: Subtract one to obtain fractions with a common numerator

question: Which of the following is the correct order of the fractions \(\dfrac{15}{11},\) \(\dfrac{19}{15},\) and \(\dfrac{17}{13},\) from least to greatest?
solution:
Each numerator is \(4\) greater than its denominator, so compare the part above \(1\):

\[
\frac{15}{11}=1+\frac4{11},\qquad
\frac{19}{15}=1+\frac4{15},\qquad
\frac{17}{13}=1+\frac4{13}.
\]

For fractions with the same positive numerator, a larger denominator gives a smaller value. Therefore

\[
\frac4{15}<\frac4{13}<\frac4{11}.
\]

Adding \(1\) preserves that order, so \(\boxed{\frac{19}{15}<\frac{17}{13}<\frac{15}{11}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). A common difference between numerator and denominator can make subtracting \(1\) more useful than finding a common denominator.
